header:
Date: 2027-10-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lydia Chen (Redwood SE), Arjun Mehta (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Pegasus CTO), Carlos Ruiz (ML Eng), Priya Rao (Security), Ellen Park (Product)
summary: Intro/discovery to understand Pegasus AI's model selection needs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Key themes: context length (32k vs 128k), multilingual support, tool/function calling and retrieval, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and security/compliance (KMS, SSO, audit logs). Customer interested in running a POC focusing on multi-lingual summarization and tool-calling integrations; ask for pricing, security docs, and schedule dedicated POC benchmarking.
topics: Context length and long-form inputs (32k vs 128k)
Open model comparisons (Llama variants, Mistral, Mixtral, MPT)
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/KMS) tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, Samir from Redwood here. um really excited to dig in, we have Lydia and Arjun from eng on the call.
[00:12] Maya Thompson: Hi thanks, Maya here, CTO at Pegasus. we wanted to cover model selection - we run summarization and multi-turn tool flows in 8 languages.
[00:22] Lydia Chen: Great, can you give us a quick sense of scale and what success looks like?
[00:28] Carlos Ruiz: Sure - roughly 1k to 5k daily active users initially, peak QPS around 100 concurrent requests, typical prompt lengths are long, many docs 20k to 80k tokens, so we're evaluating 32k-context models and the 100k-ish offerings. latency SLO is sub-2s for short prompts, for long-form we can tolerate up to 6s.
[01:05] Samir Patel: ok that helps. For the big context sizes we typically look at quantized open models - we support a number of variants on hosted and dedicated. do you have a preference for fully managed hosted vs dedicated reserved capacity?
[01:20] Maya Thompson: We're leaning dedicated because of predictability and data controls, but if hosted can meet our security needs and price we could consider it. Priya (security) will ask more on KMS and audit logs.
[01:34] Priya Rao: yeah we need customer-managed keys, SSO/SAML, and exportable audit logs. Also data residency for EU users.
[01:45] Lydia Chen: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem patterns and we have KMS/HSM integrations. Hosted supports customer KMS in the private deployment model; dedicated can be in a customer's VPC for isolation. We'll send the security pack after the call.
[02:02] Carlos Ruiz: On models - we're comparing Llama 3 70B, Mistral Instruct, Mixtral 8x, and MPT-30B with extended context. do you benchmark these?
[02:15] Arjun Mehta: We do. quick note, sometimes the names in our notes get swapped - we call Mixtral "Mixt rail" in some reports - but yes we run perf and quality profiles across models, quantization levels, and sequence lengths.
[02:29] Maya Thompson: Do you have recommendations for multilingual performance? Spanish, Portuguese, Korean, Arabic are critical.
[02:36] Lydia Chen: Historically Mistral variants and Llama-3 have strong multi-lingual footprints; for some low-resource langs you may prefer larger context or instruction-tuned checkpoints. We'll include token-level accuracy and example outputs in the POC package.
[02:55] Carlos Ruiz: Tool-calling - our flows do retrieval + external API calls; we need function calling support and deterministic routing so that a call will go to the same model variant.
[03:08] Samir Patel: Redwood supports function/tool calling patterns and deterministic routing via routing policies; we also have prefix caching and KV cache to speed repeated context. Beware the KV "cache" sometimes transcribed as K-V "cash" in docs, ha.
[03:23] Priya Rao: For compliance we need guaranteed deletion windows for KV stores - can you support retention policies and WORM?
[03:32] Lydia Chen: Yes, retention and configurable deletion windows per-customer, plus audit trails. We'll attach the retention controls doc.
[03:39] Ellen Park: On cost - what is tradeoff between 32k and 128k context models?
[03:45] Arjun Mehta: Pretty linear in memory and throughput. 128k contexts require either sharded KV or specialized sequence parallel kernels; latency goes up but we can use context-aware batching and prefix caching to reduce cost. For many use cases we recommend chunking + retrieval + summarization to keep effective context smaller.
[04:10] Maya Thompson: Any differences in accuracy if we quantize? Our ops team likes 4-bit / q4 to save costs.
[04:18] Lydia Chen: Quantization has matured; q4 and q8 give good perf for many models but may affect rare token generation and instruction following mildly. We'll run your testset across q4 and FP16 in the POC.
[04:33] Carlos Ruiz: About deployment - if we go dedicated, can we pin model versions and have canary rollouts? We have strict rollout policies.
[04:40] Samir Patel: Yes, rollouts, canaries, A/B, and automatic fallback policies are supported in Redwood Dedicated and Private. You can pin versions per-route.
[04:51] Priya Rao: For security review, we'll need SOC2 Type II evidence and an incident response SLA. Do you have past SOC2 cert?
[04:58] Lydia Chen: Yes we are SOC2 and ISO aligned; we will send certs and the incident response playbook.
[05:06] Maya Thompson: Can Redwood run on-prem? We have some air-gapped endpoints for sensitive customers.
[05:12] Arjun Mehta: Redwood Private has on-prem packaging; it's heavier lift but possible. We can do network-isolated components and local KMS.
[05:21] Carlos Ruiz: Back to models: mixing - can we run different models for different routes? e.g., Llama3 for cheap completions, Mistral for high-quality summarization, a 128k model for long docs.
[05:33] Lydia Chen: Absolutely. Smart routing lets you route by policy - latency, cost, region, or customer tier; we can also do fallback to smaller models when capacity is constrained.
[05:44] Maya Thompson: What about embeddings for retrieval? We'll need vector db support and embedding model recommendations.
[05:50] Samir Patel: We provide embeddings as a service and recommend model families for retrieval; you'll get separate cost metrics. We integrate with common vector DBs and can provide similarity benchmarks.
[06:06] Ellen Park: Any gotchas with function calling across quantized models?
[06:11] Lydia Chen: Degraded semantic parsing can happen with very aggressive quantization; we test function arg extraction in our evals but it's part of the POC to validate.
[06:23] Carlos Ruiz: For benchmarks, we'd like to run 32k summarization across Spanish and Arabic datasets - can you support multilingual tokenizer variants?
[06:34] Arjun Mehta: Yes, we map tokenization per model; for Arabic and some CJK edge cases we'll include normalization steps.
[06:44] Priya Rao: About data residency: some EU customers require data never leaves EU. Can you pin region?
[06:50] Lydia Chen: Yes, Dedicated and Private can be region-locked. Hosted can also be regionally isolated depending on plan.
[06:59] Maya Thompson: Can you share past perf numbers? like tokens/sec on A100 vs H100 for 70B and 30B?
[07:07] Samir Patel: We'll share a benchmark sheet; note our perf numbers vary by sequence length and kernel choices. We'll prepare per-model perf and cost per 1k tokens.
[07:18] Carlos Ruiz: SLA - what's uptime for Dedicated?
[07:21] Samir Patel: SLA-backed uptime with tiered guarantees; we'll include SLA doc and uptime targets.
[07:27] Ellen Park: Who will run the POC infra - us or Redwood?
[07:31] Lydia Chen: We offer assistance. For Dedicated POC usually we provision reserved nodes in Redwood Dedicated and give your team access; for Private we collaborate more to deploy. We'll outline options.
[07:45] Maya Thompson: Excellent. timeline - we want to decide vendor by end of November. We could start POC in first week of November.
[07:54] Samir Patel: That's doable. we'll aim to get pricing and security docs to you this week, schedule POC the week of Nov 1.
[08:04] Carlos Ruiz: Quick question - do you support function calling with tool results that include binary attachments? we need to pass images for OCR calls.
[08:12] Arjun Mehta: Yes, tool payloads can include multipart attachments; we have size limits and recommend external object storage links for large binaries.
[08:24] Priya Rao: On encryption at rest - we want keys rotated every 90 days; can you support rotation cadence?
[08:30] Lydia Chen: Yes KMS rotation policies supported and we can align with your cadence.
[08:36] Maya Thompson: Could you summarize next steps?
[08:39] Samir Patel: Sure - Samir to send pricing and contract, Lydia to prepare POC plan and perf checklist, Arjun will prepare benchmark scripts, Priya to send security questions, Carlos to send sample dataset.
[08:51] Ellen Park: Also include a sample SSO integration doc for our IdP (Okta).
[08:56] Lydia Chen: Will do.
[09:00] Maya Thompson: Sounds good - thanks everyone.
[09:03] Samir Patel: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with docs and a proposed POC schedule.
[09:08] [call ends]
